required.label: git present
required.prose: git must be on PATH. The workflow's mechanics are a shell script that drives git directly.

required.label: Bash present
required.prose: Bash must be available. The workflow's mechanics are a shell script.
required.fix_guidance: install Bash via your system package manager

required.label: host CLI present (where a remote exists)
required.prose: A host CLI is needed wherever the repository has a remote (gh for GitHub). git-workflow lands work by opening and merging a pull request; without the host CLI the PR path is unavailable — the workflow pushes the branch and stops.
required.fix_guidance: install the host CLI, e.g. https://cli.github.com

required.label: resolvable trunk (where a remote exists)
required.prose: git-workflow derives the branch it forks from — a local dev, a local develop, or whatever refs/remotes/origin/HEAD names — and never reads it from configuration. A repository where none of these resolves is treated as not set up, and the workflow stops rather than guess.

desirable.label: host configured for merge commits only
desirable.prose: The host should be configured for merge commits only — no squash, no rebase, no fast-forward — so landed work preserves its commit structure.
desirable.fix_command: gh api -X PATCH repos/{owner}/{repo} -F allow_squash_merge=false -F allow_rebase_merge=false

reported.label: letting the agent land its own work
reported.prose: git-workflow lands most artefacts by merging their pull request, which needs a harness permission for the merge command. Without it the agent opens the pull request and stops, leaving the artefact waiting as an open PR — deliberate, not a failure. To let the agent land unattended, allow the merge command. This is a user decision: reported, never checked pass/fail and never set.
reported.note: Add the opt-in line to .claude/settings.json (checked in, for a repository that wants it) or .claude/settings.local.json (per clone).
